newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI HEX MAY YET TOP 3,000 IN H1 - ANALYSTS. [CORRECTED 14:17 GMT]
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI HEX MAY YET TOP 3,000 IN H1 - ANALYSTS. [CORRECTED 14:17 GMT]

text.p: Despite a correction led by U.S. stocks on Friday, Finnish equities analysts said the Finnish bourse may yet have the momentum to break through 3,000 on the HEX index by summer, or perhaps sooner.
"One week of euphoria and we're there," said Mika Koskinen, analyst at Enskilda Securities.
With the HEX now close to 2,900 after setting a new all-time high of 2,903.80 on Thursday, it would only need to rise three percent to reach 3,000.
Up to Thursday's peak, Helsinki -- the smallest Nordic bourse except for Reykjavik -- had put on 16 percent this year.
In January it outperformed its Nordic neighbours, climbing over 11 percent against 10 percent for Oslo, the next best performer. It was down over one percent on Friday.

Seven of 11 analysts surveyed by Reuters said the breakthrough could easily happen by summer, with one saying it could happen in a week, another saying it would take a month, and a third saying it would take three to four months.

"We have the view that spring will be difficult ... there would still be a two percent rise in a month from now (corrects time for expected rise), but April would be a tough time," said Aktia Bank analyst Ritva Ojala.
However, for the full year Aktia expects an 11 percent rise, and the HEX will hit 3,000 points this summer, Ojala said.
Others agreed it could take up to half a year for the HEX to climb to 3,000 after any downward correction this spring. A minority saw it happening in the second half or by year-end.

And many said 3,000 as a round number might be a target for some, but does not have major technical or psychological significance, adding that Helsinki's progress hinges on trends in U.S. financial markets.
"Rising interest rates (in the U.S.) would be poison for the market," noted one.
Predicting the HEX's course has been made more difficult by the unprecedented large inflows of money into Finnish stocks since the start of the year, analysts said.
Volume in Helsinki stocks in January 1997, at 2.87 billion ECU, was more than double the year-ago total of 1.29 billion, Nordic stock exchange statistics show.

"After that strong start, we've lost some of the momentum for the whole year. It was too fast and too much," said one. But he added that fundamentals -- as opposed to demand-driven surges -- still pointed to the HEX piercing 3,000 in six to 12 months.

Jussi Hyoty at AG Private Bankers agreed: "The January rally was somewhat stronger than usual. Prices have risen fast, and it is possible that investors will now take some profits," Hyoty said. "People are getting cautious."

The HEX captures the bourse's value, but more important for trading professionals are the FOX index and the portfolio index, which caps Nokia's impact by limiting any single share's impact to no more than 10 percent, analysts said.

The FOX index, which fund managers use as a market benchmark and is the basis for derivatives exchange SOM's futures and options, rose above 1,000 points last week and has held above it since, trading on Friday at 1,008 points.
The portfolio index has roughly matched the HEX this year, with a 16 percent rise to its peak on Thursday.
Contributors to the survey: AG Private Bankers, Aktia Bank, Arctos, Aros Securities, Enskilda, Evli Securities, FIM-Rahasto Oy, FSB Securities, Merita Bank, Opstock, Postipankki.
